title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-25

ai_review.summary: Rare set with How Sweet It Is, Bo Diddley numbers and a beautiful Looks Like Rain, but plagued by splice‑filled, low‑fidelity audience recording.
ai_review.review: The concert features several historic moments – the only Dead rendition of “How Sweet It Is,” an early Bo Diddley medley, and a surprisingly pretty “Looks Like Rain.”  Unfortunately the source is a patchwork of audience tapes with splices, glitches and varying quality, making it difficult to hear the performance clearly.  Fans who value the setlist will find it worthwhile despite the technical shortcomings.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the rare songs and overall show energy (show weight high) but consistently condemn the recording quality, resulting in an average rating around 3.3; weighting yields a final AI rating of ~3.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Multiple splices and glitches; mixes of different audience sources with inconsistent levels; overall muddy, abysmal clarity making the show hard to follow.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Rare early‑show numbers and a full Bo Diddley set make for an interesting, historically significant setlist; the flow is engaging but the poor audio masks some transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Reviewers note Jerry's big grin on his face during the Bo Diddley numbers.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob delivers a heartfelt “Looks Like Rain” (LLR).
